data.name: Eadmund
data.long_meaning: Eadmund is an Old English name derived from the elements 'ead' meaning wealth and 'mund' meaning protection or prosperity. The name was popular among Anglo-Saxon rulers and saints.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing God's protection and provision in one's life.

in_hebrew.name: עדמונד
in_hebrew.meaning: אדם: אדם הראשון, תבנית, ראש, שליט, מלך
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עדמונד: שם שמוצאו מהשם האנגלי 'אדם' שקשור לאדם הראשון, שנזכר בספר בראשית. משמעותו בעברית: תבנית, ראש, שליט, ומלך. במסורת הנוצרית, שם זה קשור לעקד, המלך האגדי של אנגליה, ולנסיך האגדי 'אדוארד המובהק' של אנגליה.

in_greek.name: Εδμοντ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἐδμοντ: ὀνομαστικός τύπος τοῦ Ἐδμούντ, ὁ ὁποῖος καταγίνεται ἀπὸ τοῦ ἡνωμένου τύπου τοῦ Ἀδὰμ, πρῶτος ἄνθρωπος καὶ ἄνθρωπος. Ἐδμοντ: ἡ Ὀνομασία τοῦ παλαιότερου Ἀγγλικάνου ἡγεμόνος, ὁ ὁποῖος ἐπώνυμος τῆς Ἀγγλικῆς Ἱστορίας.

in_latin.name: Eadmundus
in_latin.long_meaning: Eadmundus: nomen gentile Anglicanum, unde Adam, primus homo, mundus, mundus. In historia Christiana, Eadmundus connotat Edmondum, regem Angliae, qui sanctus reputatur. Nomen Eadmundus significat mundum, mundum, et mundum.

in_english.name: Eadmund
in_english.meaning: man of the world, protector of the world, ruler of the world, earthly king
in_english.long_meaning: Eadmund: a name derived from the Old English name 'Eadmund', which is a compound of 'ead' meaning 'fire, noble, or earth' and 'mund' meaning 'protector, guardian, or world'. In Christian tradition, Eadmund is associated with Saint Edmund, a 9th-century king of East Anglia who was martyred by Viking invaders. The name Eadmund signifies a person who is a ruler, a protector, and a guardian of the world.

data.cultural_impact: Eadmund reflects the Anglo-Saxon values of wealth and protection, which were deeply important to their identity as a people. The use of this name among royalty and religious leaders underscores the significance of these concepts in their society.
data.spiritual_significance: Eadmund's name carries a spiritual significance as it is associated with several notable Christian saints. Saint Eadmund the King (d. 869) was a ruler of East Anglia who embraced Christianity and was later canonized. Saint Eadmund the Martyr (d. 870) was a Christian missionary in East Anglia who was executed by the Vikings and later venerated as a saint. The name Eadmund reminds us of their unwavering faith and commitment to their beliefs in the face of adversity.
